sections.content:
34,780 people

were counted on the census as "legal secretaries" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Legal secretaries file and maintain legal and other records, transcribe notes and dictation into typewritten form and perform other routine clerical tasks in legal practices.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "legal secretaries" there were more women than men (91.4% compared with 8.6%).

This means "legal secretaries" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "secretarial and related occupations".

Men made up 8.6% and women made up 91.4% of "legal secretaries"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "legal secretaries" included:

  • teaching assistants
  • occupational therapists
  • receptionists

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "legal secretaries" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "legal secretaries", 14.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "legal secretaries" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "legal secretaries" included:

  • assemblers (electrical and electronic products)
  • textiles, garments and related trades (other)
  • fishmongers and poultry dressers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "legal secretaries" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "legal secretaries" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "legal secretaries", 10.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (64.4% compared with 35.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.7%) than self-employed (2.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
